subject: Zone synchronizer + OCSP proxying for on-prem private endpoints
messages:
From: Acme Infra <infra@acme-corp.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-lead@acme-corp.com, security@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: [ACME] syncing private zone and OCSP stapling for Redwood private endpoints

Hi Rishi,

We're standing up our VPC-connected on-prem environment and need to expose several private FQDNs that point at Redwood Private endpoints. We want to avoid split-brain problems and keep certificate stapling (OCSP) healthy for long-lived client connections. High-level asks:  

- A recommended pattern for keeping our private DNS zones in sync with Redwood's control-plane records (one-way vs two-way sync).
- How you'd expect OCSP stapling to be handled when the endpoint is terminating TLS in our network (edge proxy vs. Redwood-managed OCSP responder).
- Any constraints on TTLs, SOA serial propagation, or DNSSEC interactions you expect for our setup.

We've attached a brief sketch of our proposed zone-synchronizer (push model) and a sample OCSP proxy snippet. Can we set a short technical sync to align on responsibilities?

Thanks,
Jorge Alvarez
Infra Lead, Acme Corp

Attachments: zone-sync-design.pdf (diagram), ocsp-proxy-snippet.txt (example), MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (outline)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Infra <infra@acme-corp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ACME] syncing private zone and OCSP stapling for Redwood private endpoints

Jorge — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Short answer up front: we recommend a one-way zone push from Redwood → customer-managed stub zones in most on-prem VPC cases, combined with an OCSP proxy that caches stapling responses near your edge. That gives us operational separation while avoiding two-way conflict on SOA.

High-level proposal (we'll detail in the call):
1) DNS: run a "zone-synchronizer" inside Redwood that produces signed zone deltas (IXFR-capable) and pushes them to an SFTP/HTTPS endpoint you host. Your stub-zone importer will apply deltas and expose records to your VPC resolver. This avoids AXFR race conditions and minimizes your exposure to our control-plane.

2) OCSP stapling: Redwood will continue to maintain the OCSP responder and keep short-staple lifetimes, but we recommend an OCSP-proxy cache inside your edge (TTL ~ 5 minutes, with background refresh). The proxy should present stapled responses to clients and fall back to TLS handshake without stapling if the cache is stale, while alerting on stapling misses.

3) TTLs & SOA: prefer low-ish public TTLs for the private endpoints (30–60s) during rollout and longer (300s) once steady. The SOA serialing should be monotonically increasing from Redwood's sync stream; your importer must reject out-of-order serials. If you use DNSSEC, sign locally and rotate keys independently — do not accept DNSKEY from our control plane.

Action items before our sync:
- Jorge: confirm an HTTPS endpoint and a service account for zone-delta pulls.
- Karthik: I'll loop you for the OCSP proxy sample and the exact stapling semantics we'll expose.
- Marissa: please add a checklist for audit evidence (OCSP logs, zone delta hashes).

I can meet tomorrow at 10am PT — if that works for you we'll send a calendar invite.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

(Attachment references retained)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ACME] syncing private zone and OCSP stapling for Redwood private endpoints

Jorge / team — added a few engineering details we should consider. Quick, concrete notes: 

- Zone sync mechanics: prefer signed JSON deltas over raw AXFR if your importer can't support IXFR. Each delta should carry a monotonic vector (serial, timestamp, hash). We will provide a rotation-signed manifest so you can verify authenticity.

- One-way push benefits: no split-brain, clear ownership. Downside: you cannot edit records on your side without requesting a Redwood change. If you need local overrides we recommend CNAME-based local overrides rather than two-way sync.

- OCSP Proxy behavior:
  * Cache window: 300s refresh window recommended for high-availability edges; serve stapling if cached response is <= 5m old, else trigger background refresh and serve last-known-good while warning.
  * Responder timeouts: backend calls to Redwood's OCSP responder should have 250ms timeout; proxy should circuit-break after three failures.
  * Logging: proxy must log responder status, stapling freshness, and stapling-failure counts for audit. We will accept those logs for SOC evidence.

- Certificate rotation: Redwood will push CRL/OCSP revocation events via the same delta channel. Please ensure your importer treats revocation deltas as high-priority (apply within 60s).

I've attached a short ocsp-proxy-snippet.txt showing the refresh loop and verification checks. Happy to walk through it in the call.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference
